summary: CMS finalized its 2027 outpatient rule on Nov. 4, adding imaging at off-campus hospital outpatient departments to site-neutral payment and removing 637 more services from the inpatient-only list. Health systems keep building outpatient capacity, but with tighter capital discipline and phased projects. On the marketing side, new Edelman and LinkedIn research shows executives use AI to digest thought leadership and share it privately inside buying groups, which favors data-rich, shareable content.

topStories.title: CMS finalizes 2027 outpatient rule: site-neutral pay expands to off-campus imaging
topStories.summary: Outpatient rates rise 2.3%. Imaging without contrast at excepted off-campus provider-based departments moves to the lower physician fee schedule rate, saving an estimated $260 million in 2027. CMS removes 637 services from the inpatient-only list and adds several hundred procedures to the ASC covered list.
topStories.whyItMatters: Off-campus imaging economics change in 2027, and more procedures can move to ASCs. Health systems will revisit where imaging and surgery sit in their outpatient real estate.

topStories.title: AHA calls site-neutral expansion and inpatient-only phase-out misguided
topStories.summary: The AHA says the payment update does not reflect hospitals' financial challenges and warns that 340B cuts and accelerated clawbacks will add strain, especially for rural and underserved communities.
topStories.whyItMatters: Margin pressure on hospital outpatient departments raises interest in lower-cost sites of care and in real estate structures that protect capital.

topStories.title: Hospital closures pick up late in 2026
topStories.summary: Becker's has tracked nine hospital and emergency department closures this year, three of them added the week of Nov. 9. HCA Florida Pasadena Hospital will end inpatient care and shift to emergency care. More than 40% of rural hospitals operate at a loss, per the Chartis Center for Rural Health.
topStories.whyItMatters: Inpatient-to-outpatient conversions and rural access gaps create openings for right-sized outpatient and emergency facilities.

topStories.title: Hospital M&A in 2026 already exceeds all of 2025
topStories.summary: Kaufman Hall counted 56 announced hospital deals in the first nine months of 2026, versus 46 in all of 2025. Larger systems are buying capabilities, not just scale, and joint ventures are growing, such as Duke Health and CaroMont Health in Charlotte.
topStories.whyItMatters: Newly combined systems rationalize facilities and build new outpatient networks in the first two years after a deal.

topStories.title: The ambulatory boom is far from over, CEOs say
topStories.summary: Outpatient services were 57% of hospital revenue in 2024, up from 52% in 2020, and Sg2 projects 17% outpatient volume growth over the next decade. Main Line Health, Saint Anthony Hospital and FirstHealth of the Carolinas are building integrated outpatient campuses and medical office buildings.
topStories.whyItMatters: Demand for outpatient campuses and medical office buildings keeps growing, which is Boldt's core work.

topStories.title: CEOs sharpen discipline on capital investments
topStories.summary: Health systems are still investing but phasing projects so they can pause if reimbursement worsens. Atlantic Health split a $90 million operating room expansion into four phases. Broward Health approved nearly $1 billion for freestanding EDs, medical office buildings and practice growth.
topStories.whyItMatters: Phased projects and off-balance-sheet options matter more when boards scrutinize every capital dollar.

trends.title: Outpatient growth with tighter capital
trends.detail: Systems keep expanding ambulatory care while splitting projects into phases and protecting cash. Development partners that can phase work and offer financing options fit how boards are deciding.

trends.title: Site of care keeps shifting
trends.detail: The 2027 rule extends site-neutral payment to off-campus imaging and keeps moving procedures off the inpatient-only list and onto the ASC list. Expect more ASC joint ventures and imaging relocations.

trends.title: Growth across state lines, starting small
trends.detail: Kaiser Permanente, UPMC, Northwell and Sutter are entering new states, often with outpatient and primary care sites before hospitals.

trends.title: Construction spending keeps rising
trends.detail: ConstructConnect projects hospital and clinic construction will reach $38.8 billion by 2030, and medical office, outpatient surgery and imaging buildings will grow about 5% a year to $10.5 billion.

items.title: Why Kaiser, UPMC, Northwell are crossing state lines in 2026
items.summary: Cross-market deals carry less antitrust risk and more payer leverage. Northwell is entering Pennsylvania with smaller primary and immediate care sites first.

items.title: The ambulatory boom is far from over, CEOs say
items.summary: Outpatient revenue share and volumes keep rising; several systems are building integrated outpatient campuses and medical office buildings.

items.title: Health system projects worth $500M or more in 2026
items.summary: Large projects include Novant Health's Wilmington expansion with a medical office building and rehabilitation hospital, and Baptist Health South Florida's new Sunrise hospital.

items.title: Hospital mergers in 2026 exceed last year
items.summary: 56 announced deals in nine months, including Sutter Health and Allina Health and Prisma Health and Erlanger Health System.

items.title: CEOs sharpen discipline on capital investments
items.summary: Systems are phasing projects and prioritizing must-haves rather than stopping investment.

items.title: Hospital construction spending forecast to 2030
items.summary: Construction starts expected to reach about $30.7 billion in 2026; 45% of executives are raising the share of capital for new hospital construction.

items.title: CMS finalizes 2027 outpatient and ASC rule
items.summary: 2.3% update, site-neutral payment for off-campus imaging, 637 services off the inpatient-only list, several hundred procedures added to the ASC list.

items.title: AHA statement on the 2027 outpatient rule
items.summary: AHA opposes the site-neutral expansion, inpatient-only phase-out and 340B cuts.

items.title: 6 healthcare workforce trends to watch
items.summary: RN turnover was 17.6% in 2025, costing the average hospital $5.19 million a year. Systems are rehiring former staff and moving to targeted pay.

items.title: Hospital closures ramp up as 2026 nears end
items.summary: Nine closures tracked this year, three added the week of Nov. 9; some hospitals are converting to emergency-only care.

items.title: 2026 Edelman-LinkedIn B2B Thought Leadership Impact Report
items.summary: 84% of B2B decision-makers used AI to summarize thought leadership during vendor evaluation. 89% shared it through private channels, and 56% said showing an understanding of their challenges most raised their confidence in a company, versus 14% for product strengths.
items.takeaway: Lead with the client's constraints and data they can forward, not service lists.

items.title: LinkedIn shares key trends in B2B marketing
items.summary: 75% of decision-makers say thought leadership is a more reliable way to judge a company than marketing materials. Employee networks are about 12 times larger than company followings, and LinkedIn recommends Thought Leader Ads.
items.takeaway: Test Thought Leader Ads from Boldt leaders alongside company ads.

items.title: Gartner 2026 CMO Spend Survey
items.summary: Marketing budgets average 7.8% of revenue, with 15.3% of marketing budgets going to AI, but only 30% of CMOs say they are ready to scale AI.
items.takeaway: Put AI into narrow, measurable workflows before scaling it.

items.title: 95% of B2B marketers use AI, fewer than 4 in 10 say it is working
items.summary: Buying committees for deals over $50,000 average 11.2 people, and buyers review 13.4 pieces of content before contacting a vendor.
items.takeaway: Plan content for every member of the buying group, not just one contact.

items.title: Zero-click searches hit 72% where AI Overviews appear
items.summary: A field experiment found zero-click searches rose from 54% to 72% on queries with AI Overviews, and organic clicks fell 38%. Brand websites make up only 5 to 10% of the sources AI search cites.
items.takeaway: Structure pages with clear answers, FAQs and schema, and earn mentions on third-party sites AI tools trust.
